title: Mouse Without Borders fails to resynchronize after minutes

judgment.rationale: The symptom is clear: resynchronization fails until restart, but the attached diagnostic archive was invalid, so socket error and machine-state evidence are missing. The reconnect and power/network event paths are identifiable, making this a red-confidence investigation rather than a ready implementation.
judgment.recommended_action: Obtain a valid post-reproduction diagnostic report and correlate socket reopen, network availability, and machine-pool state before changing reconnect behavior.

evidence.fact: The reporter says Mouse Without Borders stops resynchronizing after several minutes and only restart repairs it.
The submitted diagnostic archive could not be analyzed as valid evidence.
InitAndCleanup schedules socket reopening on network availability and power-mode events, coordinated with Common.Sk and SocketStuff.

fix_assessment.rationale: Reconnect/state recovery is a valid design target, but there is no usable trace showing whether the failure is socket, peer, authentication, or stale machine-state.

proposed_fixes.title: Make Mouse Without Borders recovery reset stale transport state
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The restart-only recovery symptom is consistent with a stale socket or connection state surviving the existing reopen triggers, but the failing state is not yet identified.
plan: Correlate socket read/write failures, network availability events, and machine-pool state transitions.
Reset or recreate only the stale transport state after a confirmed recoverable failure.
Add bounded retry/backoff and a diagnostic event that identifies why synchronization was reset.
verification: The captured failure recovers without restarting PowerToys.
Repeated network interruption and resume tests do not leave a stale synchronized/unsynchronized state.
Intentional disconnect and peer authentication remain stable.

confidence.rationale: The symptom strongly suggests recovery-state handling, but the invalid diagnostics leave the exact state machine failure unknown.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders loses synchronization after running for minutes and recovers only after restart.
known_information: The issue provides a clear duration-dependent symptom.
A diagnostic archive was attached but is invalid for analysis.
The repository has explicit network/power-triggered socket reopening paths.
inferences: A stale socket or machine-pool state may survive a recoverable network failure.
The restart workaround suggests recovery state is not fully reset.
issue_context.analysis: Capture a valid report at the first failed sync and compare socket lifecycle events with peer connectivity and state resets.

information_gaps.information: The first failure timestamp, affected peer count, whether both machines remain connected, and socket reopen/error events.
information_gaps.why_needed: Without this evidence a reconnect change could mask authentication or peer-state problems.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce until synchronization fails, run /bugreport on both sides if possible, and record the first failure time and whether restarting only one side recovers it.

actions.label: Request targeted evidence
actions.note: Replace the invalid archive with a time-correlated report and isolate the recovery boundary.

comment.body: The symptom is actionable, but the previously attached diagnostic archive was invalid, so there is no socket or peer-state evidence to distinguish a stale connection from a machine-pool/authentication problem. Please reproduce until synchronization first fails, record the approximate time and whether one or both machines are affected, then run /bugreport immediately on the affected side (and the peer if possible). Please state whether restarting only one side restores sync; this is the key recovery discriminator.

actions.label: Approve focused fix design
actions.note: The proposed design is specific enough for fork-side implementation after maintainer approval.

design.scope: Trace and reset the Mouse Without Borders reconnect state at the first recoverable transport failure without disrupting intentional disconnects.
acceptance_criteria: A transient network/socket failure restores synchronization without process restart.
The first failure produces a bounded, actionable diagnostic event.
Peer authentication and intentional disconnect behavior are unchanged.
